_meta.purpose: External psychophysics / perceptual-decision-making code samples to broaden the empirical base behind v0.2 lens tuning. Companion to db/csnl-conventions.json (which is CSNL-internal). Sources: GitHub public repos + OSF deposits + paper supplementaries.
_meta.harness: Five parallel isolated general-purpose subagents (model=opus, read-only browse + WebSearch/WebFetch + shallow git clones to /tmp/). Each agent owned one lab roster (Gardner / Acerbi / Stocker / Sims / Adjacent), produced a Markdown report with structured per-sample fields, orchestrator transcribed into this JSON.
_meta.scope_note: A 'sample' here is one experiment-running script OR one paper-companion data+model package. Framework-only repos (mgl, ToolboxToolbox, snow-dots, PsychoJS itself) are listed in reference_frameworks but not as samples.

provenance.orchestrator: Claude Opus 4.7 (claude-opus-4-7[1m]) running in CSNL lab Claude Code session
primary_sources_used: https://www.sas.upenn.edu/~astocker/ (lab page; no per-paper code link)
notes: All cloned trees are shallow (git clone --depth=1) and live under /tmp/ — not committed to this repo.
Per-sample evidence fields cite real file:line refs within those clones; URLs cited above are the canonical upstream sources for verification.
The Sims agent burned 132 tool calls because the Sims lab does NOT publish on its own org (simsc3 is empty) — the agent had to identify active student handles via paper citation chasing.
No data was modified at any of the cited URLs. All reads were read-only / shallow-clone-and-Read.
Replicability: re-run via scripts/scan-external-samples.md harness. Expect numbers to drift as labs publish new repos.

sims.specialty_finding: Despite Sims's theoretical focus on rate-distortion / continuous-report delayed-estimation, ALL 4 inspected Sims-lab artifacts use forced-choice keypress responses. The 'color wheel mouse-drag' delayed-estimation mechanism standard in Wilken/Bays literature does NOT appear in any reachable Sims-lab repo. Theory-practice mismatch is itself a finding.

release_shape_taxonomy.implication: External-host / frontend-not-released is a recognizable release shape across labs. Lens MUST handle this (see PTB lens § External-host pattern) and not penalize as 'incomplete'.

key_observations_for_lens_tuning_v0_2: ONE-ENGINE-MANY-RUNNERS pattern (Pelli CriticalSpacing, Brainard) — when a repo has <Name>.m + 10+ run<Variant>.m wrappers, each run*.m is a separate experiment variant.
BIG one-struct config pattern (o.* / params.* / settings struct) — every lab has this; emit as parameters[] block.
JSON/CSV-driven block sequence (Gold) — DefaultBlockSequence.csv adjacent to run_task.m means external schedule (CSV).
ToolboxToolbox descriptor (<RepoName>.json at repo root with 'type':'git'/'include') — the REAL entry call is tbUseProject('<name>') BEFORE run_task.m.
snow-dots OOP scheduler (Gold) — classdef topsTreeNodeTask* + topNode.run() + dotsReadable* input plugins. Distinct from PTB and mgl.

Adaptive procedure pluggability: distinguish QUEST (Watson 1983), QUEST+ (qpInitialize), PSI (Kontsevich-Tyler / psybayes), generic up-down staircase (doStaircase), Bayesian info-max (DG BAM). Each has a different file signature.
Eye-tracker pluggability: 'readables' cell-list or input-device array → surface as hardware_inputs field. Gold's enumeration (Eyelink/PupilLabs/EOG/Gamepad/Keyboard/Mouse-sim) is canonical.
Cross-session state persisted as .mat (HVI) — <INIT>_<sess>.mat in per-subject folder holds POSTERIOR across sessions, not just data. Distinguish 'raw-data save' from 'state-carry save'.
License heterogeneity (MIT / Apache-2.0 / GPL-3.0 / LGPL-3.0 / NONE) — warn on license=null samples for reuse risk.
Framework-only repos (mgl, snow-dots, BrainardLabToolbox, psychopy-pixx) — filter on 'has at least one entry script that calls Screen/visual.Window/mglOpen', not just on lab affiliation.
Subject-id conventions: 3-letter codes (CWG), zero-padded numerics (10_), uppercase (HVI subject IDs), per-subject folder. Multiple styles — recognize all.
Replay mode (Gardner afcom, afmap) — first-class feature for offline re-rendering. Tag scripts with replay=arg parsing.
Two-stage seed (CSNL HJL: rand draws seed → seed pinned downstream) vs. one-stage (rng(seed_literal)) vs. unseeded fallback (PsychoJS Math.random) — three distinct reproducibility surfaces.
CSNL between-subject CB via participants.csv is RARE in adjacent labs; lens should still detect it but not penalize absence.
Sims's 'continuous-report color-wheel delayed-estimation' is NOT in any released code despite theory focus — don't pattern-match on theory keywords for code-level detection.
Stocker's release shape (data+model, no stimulus code, MIT/none) is a valid 'paper-companion' class — lens must not score it as 'incomplete experiment'.

harness_design.team_composition: 5 parallel general-purpose subagents (model=opus), one per lab roster (Gardner / Acerbi / Stocker / Sims / Adjacent). Each independent context, ~5-12 min wall-clock.
harness_design.tools_per_agent: WebSearch, WebFetch, Bash (read-only + git clone into /tmp/), Read, Grep, Glob
harness_design.scope_per_agent: one lab; ≥3-12 samples; for each sample: shallow clone, read entry + README, characterize per structured fields, cite source+file:line
harness_design.orchestrator_collation: transcribe per-sample blocks into this JSON; aggregate cross-lab patterns into cross_lab_findings; record skipped labs + reasons
harness_design.rerun_cadence: annual or when new prominent labs publish open-source experiment code; not coupled to CSNL roster changes
what_NOT_to_do: don't dispatch one agent across all labs at once (context pollution)
don't classify framework-only repos (mgl, BrainardLabToolbox) as experiment samples
don't classify data+model packages as 'incomplete experiments' — they are a valid release shape
don't double-count borrowed datasets (Stocker Speed_Prior 2022 reuses NN2006 SUB1-5)
don't conflate cosmic-name homonyms (Princeton economist Christopher A. Sims ≠ RPI cognitive scientist Chris R. Sims)
